title: Steering-sunset retro step
description:
In skills/ticks/references/agent-runner.md: add a new retro step 6, "Steering sunset". The old step 6 (Retro report) becomes 7 and the old step 7 (Configured close-out steps) becomes 8. Fix "It takes 7 steps" and every pointer to the old numbers (e.g. the run-start bullet that says "step 7"). Add one bullet to the Retro report list for the sunset tally.

The step must say:
- The tally comes from the implementer reports' per-check lines (labels and outcomes per the shared vocabulary).
- "Caught" means `went red and changed the code`. `went red, not from this change` is recorded but is not a catch. An epic where a check was only `not applicable` counts neither way.
- The prior epic's tally is read from the previous retro report.
- A check with no catch for two consecutive epics is demoted in `.tick/config.md` `## Testing` from every tick to "where the logic warrants". The retro applies the demotion and the report records it with its evidence.
- Harness checks (the wave gate, the final review, the DoD, the checkpoint) are never candidates.
- Rework found at the wave gate or final review in a demoted check's domain restores the check (the sunset runs in reverse).
- The point, in one line: harness checks stay constant; the model re-verifying itself shrinks on evidence.
- Scope: the tally covers only checks that claim to catch something and carry a report line: `## Testing` tick-gate commands, `by-path run`, and `planted fault`. Checks a project mandates through `.tick/config.md` `## Rules` are human intent held constant. They are changed by the human and never demoted by the retro. (Settled with the spec author.)

Shared vocabulary (verbatim across all three parallel chains, which do not see each other):
- Files: `.tick/learnings.md` is the always-read head (at most 4096 bytes: hard rules plus an index of the body's categories). `.tick/learnings-ref.md` is the looked-up body (Problem/Cause/Rule entries, at most 16384 bytes, at most 800 bytes per entry). The 800-byte entry limit applies to the body only. The engine owns the format; the project owns the content.
- Check labels in implementer reports: the tick-gate command verbatim, `by-path run`, `planted fault`.
- Check outcomes: `ran clean`, `went red and changed the code`, `went red, not from this change`, `not applicable`.
- Terms: "parallel warm-chains", "warm turn", "retire" (an implementer is retired after the final review).
- Existing section titles in agent-runner.md stay as they are. The gate names are "tick gate" and "wave gate", already defined.
Spec (source of truth): docs/thoughts/2026-11-12-lean-epics.md. Edit only skills/ticks/ (never an installed copy) unless your task names other files. Keep the engine's terse voice; criteria, not step lists.
